Lighting: clear afternoon daylight through the trees, warm highlights and cool green shadows. Quiet mountain air, with a sense of hidden depth beyond the clearing. Opaque full-frame scenery.

Use case: historical-scene.

Primary request: an ancient Greek sanctuary just above the Argive shore. A broad weathered limestone altar stands slightly left of center, with suppliant olive branches bound with white wool resting against its low stepped base. A simple stone basin sits nearby. A small Doric shrine and an olive tree shelter one side of the court. Beyond the low sea-facing wall, blue coastal water and a single small distant wooden sailing ship are visible. To the right of the altar, an open shore gate leads to a clearly visible path toward modest sunlit town houses and their sheltered doorways. Low Greek hills frame the distance.
Composition: eye level, wide 16:9. The altar, bound branches and open route toward shelter stay readable in the central phone crop. Keep generous open paving and sandy ground across the lower third for separate cast portraits. Give the path a clear line from the altar through the gate toward the homes. Architecture and coastal landscape fill the painting.
Style: richly detailed painted Greek storybook realism, aged limestone, soft ochre plaster, natural olive green, wool and clay textures, clear blue water. The sanctuary feels like a living refuge where a city's promise becomes practical care.
Lighting: clear warm afternoon daylight, gentle shadows, calm dry air. Opaque full-frame scenery.
